description: No Backbase, Mambu, Finastra or Thought Machine page naming a Slovenian bank was found in this pass, in either English or Slovene queries.

result.result_summary: Searches combining these vendors with NLB / Nova KBM / SKB / Slovenia returned only generic product comparison pages and bank-merger news, no vendor customer story.

why_it_matters: Absence of a public reference does not mean absence of a deal — these vendors sell into CEE and may be under NDA or announce only via partner channels. The vendor pages should remain on the monitoring list rather than being written off.

description: Global core-banking vendors publish essentially nothing in Slovene; local-language queries surfaced local vendors (HRC, SETCCE, Halcom) and press, but no sl-language page on temenos.com, backbase.com, mambu.com or finacle.com.

result.result_summary: Slovene queries ('jedrni bančni sistem', 'referenčna zgodba', 'prenova informacijskega sistema') returned local vendors, local press and academic theses only.

why_it_matters: For this cell the local-language channel is productive for the LOCAL vendor tier and for incident-driven disclosure, while the global-vendor tier must be tracked in English. Collection design should split accordingly.

description: The Mambu customer-story index URL was inferred from standard vendor site structure and was not confirmed by a fetch in this pass.

result.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence (0.45); no claim of liveness is made.

why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification must resolve the actual customer-story path before this source is relied upon.

description: No Worldline, Nexi or NCR Atleos case study naming a Slovenian bank was located; the SI link to that tier runs through Bankart's partnership with Nets (now part of Nexi) reported in trade press rather than through a vendor case study.

result.result_summary: Vendor self-service/payments case-study libraries surfaced CEE examples (CSOB) but no SI institution.

why_it_matters: For payments-processing intelligence in SI, the processor (Bankart) and trade press are more productive entry points than the vendors' own case-study libraries.

description: No public announcement was found naming a specific card issuing/acquiring platform vendor behind Bankart's card processing (e.g. OpenWay Way4, TSYS, Tietoevry). Only the SEPA/instant central infrastructure has a named external supplier (Nets) in the sources found.

result.result_summary: Vendor searches returned generic vendor marketing pages plus one Bankart–Nets infrastructure story; no SI card-platform reference page surfaced.

why_it_matters: The identity of the card management system under Slovenia's national processor is the single most valuable unknown for this cell; its absence must not be filled by assumption.

description: No Slovenia-specific Visa or Mastercard processor certification or principal-membership announcement was found for 2025-2026 in open search.

result.result_summary: Scheme searches returned only generic global licensing/certification guidance pages.

why_it_matters: Scheme certification announcements were assumed to be a primary public trace for this cell; they appear to be published mostly via scheme directories rather than press releases, shifting collection toward directory scraping.

description: Slovenian-language terminology for tokenisation is thin: searches on tokenizacija/žetoniziranje kartic produced no dedicated SI vendor or bank technical page in this pass; SI sources use English terms or describe the capability functionally (mobilno kartično plačevanje, digitalna denarnica).

result.result_summary: Tokenisation as a named local-language concept has no distinct SI source footprint found.

why_it_matters: Tokenisation supplier identity (scheme TSP vs. processor-hosted) stays unmapped for SI, and the local glossary lacks a reliable query term for it.

description: A reference surfaced to the historical 'Transact-EON' authorisation network linking Bankart, Banka Koper and Plasis, and to legacy SI card brands (Activa, Karanta). No current authoritative page was located for these.

result.result_summary: Mentioned only in a low-quality secondary aggregation; historical status unverified.

why_it_matters: Legacy switch/brand names are useful archival query terms for reconstructing SI switching history but must be treated as unverified until a primary source is found.

description: Euronet is named by a secondary source as an acquiring-processing provider in Slovenia alongside Bankart and Cetis, but no Euronet Slovenia acquiring/processing page was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Actor plausible but not sourced to a primary page.

why_it_matters: Euronet is a significant ATM/acquiring processor regionally; leaving it unmapped would understate the competitive set.

description: Margento and Halcom, both Slovenian payment-technology names, returned no payments-platform or tokenisation evidence under the combined query used.

result.result_summary: Query conflated three companies; only Paywiser returned substantive results.

why_it_matters: Halcom (e-banking/qualified certificates) and Margento (mobile payments) are plausible SI payments-adjacent vendors that remain unassessed; they need dedicated single-entity queries.

description: Fetched https://www.money-motion.eu/expo/ directly. Despite claiming 30+ exhibitors and 2,000 m2 of expo space, the page names no exhibitor or sponsor at all — it is a promotional landing page with a lead-capture form.

result.result_summary: Exhibitor census for the most important regional payments event is not machine-readable from the expo page; it must be reconstructed from the event mobile app, the separate /sponsors/ page (logo images), and post-event press coverage.

why_it_matters: Exhibitor lists are the completest vendor censuses in this cell; if the primary site withholds them, collection must be multi-source and will be lossier.

description: Searched in Slovenian for a standalone Slovenian payments/cards conference (konferenca plačila, plačilni promet, kartično poslovanje) analogous to Croatia's Money Motion. None was found. The closest is the ZBS internal posvetovanje o kartičnem poslovanju, which is a member consultation rather than a public trade fair with an exhibitor floor.

result.result_summary: Slovenia appears to have no independent public payments trade fair; vendor visibility flows instead through ZBS member events, general IT conferences (DSI, INFOSEK, NT) and the regional Money Motion in Zagreb.

why_it_matters: Collection strategy must accept that Slovenian payments-vendor visibility is distributed across generic IT events and a foreign regional event, not concentrated in one national show.

description: ZBS pages for Bančna konferenca and the professional consultations describe programme and audience but no sponsor/partner tier was surfaced in this pass. Similarly, no sponsor list was surfaced for Dnevi zavarovalništva v Sloveniji.

result.result_summary: Industry-association events in SI appear to run on membership fees rather than visible sponsor tiers, so 'paid declaration of intent' signal is weaker here than at commercial conferences.

why_it_matters: For ZBS/SZZ events the usable signal is the speaker/panel roster and post-event write-ups, not sponsorship; collection rules should differ per event type.

description: Search results attribute the Netko award both to Slovensko društvo Informatika (historically) and to GZS together with Register.si (current). The official netko.si site was not fetched in this pass to resolve the discrepancy.

result.result_summary: Netko stewardship is unresolved; recorded as a hypothesis, not a fact.

why_it_matters: Getting the organiser wrong misroutes collection and misattributes the award's credibility.

description: WEBSI awards were only evidenced through media coverage (siol.net, metropolitan.si, zurnal24, branddna.si, superznamka.si). The canonical WEBSI domain (websi.si) was inferred, not fetched or confirmed.

result.result_summary: WEBSI recorded with confidence 0.6 and access_status unverified pending a liveness check.

why_it_matters: The winners archive is the durable artefact; if the official site does not host one, the media mirrors become the primary source.

description: No established Slovenian-language term or dedicated venue was found for a 'payments trade fair' / 'exhibitor list' in the financial-sector sense. 'Razstavljavci' returns results only for general IT/security events (INFOSEK, CYBER & INFOSECURITY), never for banking events.

result.result_summary: Local-language vocabulary for this cell is borrowed from the general IT-event domain, which shapes which queries can work.

why_it_matters: Query design for future runs should route through IT-event vocabulary plus bank-audience filters rather than payments-fair vocabulary, which does not exist locally.

description: Searched for an 'SBC digital summit' with fintech sponsors/exhibitors; SBC (Klub slovenskih podjetnikov) runs webinars and press conferences but no fintech-focused summit with a published exhibitor roster was found.

result.result_summary: SBC downgraded to an indirect, low-priority source (member directory and event partners only).

why_it_matters: Prevents over-weighting a cell seed that does not correspond to a real exhibitor-bearing event.

description: Direct Slovene queries for a bank switching core-banking supplier ('slovenska banka zamenjala ponudnika bancnega sistema', 'jedrni bancni sistem') returned no press article naming a supplier switch - only Banka Slovenije regulatory pages plus consumer-impact coverage of the BKS Bank migration.

result.result_summary: Zero direct vendor-switch stories surfaced via general web search; the only migration evidence is indirect (customer harm reporting).

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale in reverse: Slovenian press does cover these events, but almost never as procurement stories - they surface as outage/complaint stories. Collection keyword sets must therefore target failure symptoms (trajniki, izpiski, napake, prenova sistema, migracija), not procurement vocabulary.

description: Finance.si, the outlet most likely to carry contract values and displaced-incumbent detail, did not surface any relevant article through open web search; its content appears to sit behind subscription and is poorly indexed for this topic.

result.result_summary: Seed query aimed at Finance.si returned unrelated vendor and Banka Slovenije pages, no Finance.si article.

why_it_matters: The highest-value source in this cell is effectively invisible to open search. Without a subscription plus site-native search, the run will systematically under-report Slovenian deal detail.

description: Attempted to locate dedicated Slovenian IT/B2B trade blogs beyond Monitor and Racunalniske novice (searched for Poslovni svet, Slotech-type community/trade sites). No additional Slovene-language banking-IT trade blog was confirmed; the one strong match returned was Croatian (ICTbusiness.info).

result.result_summary: Slovenian IT trade-media landscape appears to be a narrow two-to-three outlet field, not a blog ecosystem.

why_it_matters: Reduces expected source count for this cell and raises the weight that must be placed on Monitor/Monitor Pro, Racunalniske novice and vendor-published journals.

description: The Moje finance URL was inferred from the Casnik Finance publisher structure rather than confirmed in a search result; only the publisher relationship was confirmed (via the Slovene Wikipedia entry on Finance).

result.result_summary: Publisher confirmed, exact subdomain not confirmed.

why_it_matters: Flagged so the deterministic liveness pass treats this URL as a hypothesis and falls back to finance.si site navigation if it fails.

description: Targeted search of SeeNews for Slovenian banking *technology* contracts returned only M&A, bond and financing items — no IT/vendor-selection stories surfaced.

result.result_summary: SeeNews Slovenia coverage is deal/financial rather than technology-procurement oriented; its tech section is separate and mostly IT-company M&A (e.g. Actual I.T.).

why_it_matters: SeeNews should be tracked as an ownership/M&A early-warning source, not as a vendor-win feed; expecting contract news from it will produce false coverage confidence.

description: No Slovenia-specific banking or payments vendor item could be surfaced on emerging-europe.com through search in this run.

result.result_summary: Emerging Europe is listed in the cell brief but produced zero verified Slovenian banking-vendor articles in the queries run; its relevance remains unproven.

why_it_matters: Priority for Emerging Europe should stay provisional until a site-internal search confirms Slovenian financial-sector coverage volume.

description: Slovenian-language search using procurement/selection phrasing ('banka ... izbrala ponudnika ... plačilni sistem ... pogodba') returned only regulator and collective-agreement pages, no news of a bank selecting a technology vendor.

result.result_summary: Vendor-selection announcements are apparently not phrased this way in Slovenian public web content, or are published only as vendor-side English press releases.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: the English trade-press/newswire channel is genuinely load-bearing for Slovenian vendor-win intelligence; sl-language phrasing needs different anchors (e.g. 'prenova jedrnega bančnega sistema', 'javno naročilo', 'implementacija rešitve').

description: Tracxn company/deal detail is gated behind account creation and its ToS restricts automated collection.

result.result_summary: Only aggregate counts (136 Slovenian fintech entities, 29 funded) are visible without login.

why_it_matters: Directory value is real but cannot be harvested programmatically without a licence; plan for manual or licensed use.

description: No dedicated Slovenian- or Croatian-language regional fintech trade outlet was identified in this run that systematically covers bank technology procurement across the Adriatic.

result.result_summary: Regional coverage appears to be split between English trade press (Finextra, FinTech Futures, Paypers) and country-level general business media; no Adriatic banking-technology trade title found.

why_it_matters: Means cross-border vendor tracking must be assembled from several English sources plus vendor newsrooms rather than one regional title.

description: Searched in Slovenian for public service-status / incident pages for SI payment infrastructure (Bankart, Flik, bank online banking). No dedicated status.* page or machine-readable incident feed was located; Bankart directs users to email/phone support and banks publish outage notices as ad-hoc news items.

result.result_summary: No status.bankart.si-style page discovered; only support and product pages plus per-bank notice sections.

why_it_matters: Status pages are usually the cheapest real-time deployment/incident signal. Their apparent absence means outage-based inference must fall back on bank news pages, app-store reviews and forum reports, which are noisier and slower.

description: Explicit searches (sl and en) for SI bank job ads naming Temenos T24, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra, Mambu, Backbase or similar returned no Slovenian ad. Results were dominated by non-SI content and generic vendor-comparison articles.

result.result_summary: Zero confirmed SI vacancy naming a specific core-banking product in this discovery pass.

why_it_matters: This is a discovery-method limitation, not evidence that such ads do not exist: search engines index SI job boards poorly and ads expire quickly. It argues for on-site crawling of the boards themselves rather than relying on web search.

description: Careers/job pages were confirmed for Bankart; equivalents for Halcom, SRC d.o.o. and Asseco SEE Slovenia were not surfaced by the searches performed in this pass.

result.result_summary: Only Bankart's vendor careers section confirmed.

why_it_matters: Integrator-side hiring (Halcom, SRC, Asseco) is often the earliest signal of a bank project win; missing those pages leaves a hole on the supply side of the cell.

description: All candidates were identified via search-result evidence; individual URLs were not fetched one-by-one in this pass, so reachability is unverified by design.

result.result_summary: URLs recorded with confidence scores, not liveness claims.

why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must run before any URL is treated as live; treat 403/timeouts as bot defence rather than death.

description: No published, itemised list of Slovenian FDI-screening decisions (priglasitve neposrednih tujih naložb) was found; searches surfaced only the legal framework and law-firm commentary.

result.result_summary: Framework pages and advisories found; per-transaction decision list not located.

why_it_matters: Foreign acquisitions of SI payment vendors below AVK thresholds may leave no public per-deal trace, so this channel cannot be relied on for deal detection.

description: No evidence found of any ownership change at Bankart d.o.o.; searches show it remains owned by a consortium of SI banks (NLB, OTP banka, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Deželna banka).

result.result_summary: Aggregator profiles list bank shareholders; no acquisition or exit reported.

why_it_matters: The central SI processor being bank-owned rather than group-owned means consolidation pressure arrives via its bank shareholders, not via a vendor takeover.

description: AVK decision PDFs are individually linked under a fileadmin path; no machine-readable index or API was identified during this run.

result.result_summary: HTML decision listing found; structured feed not found.

why_it_matters: Collection will need HTML scraping plus PDF parsing rather than a clean feed; brittleness risk.

description: Primary SI business-press deal reporting (Finance.si) and the payment yearbook are behind paywalls; not fetched.

result.result_summary: Access restricted; status is a hypothesis, not verified dead.

why_it_matters: Earliest deal signals often appear in paid press, so budget or licensed access materially affects timeliness.

description: No Slovenian country page, local legal entity, office or named Slovenian distributor could be found for Glory Global Solutions, Auriga SpA or KEBA, despite searches in both English and Slovenian. Diebold Nixdorf's indexed EMEA locations path for the region returned a 404-style title, suggesting the directory moved rather than that coverage ended.

result.result_summary: Searches returned only global corporate pages and non-Slovenian references (KEBA references are Austrian/German Sparkassen and Erste; Auriga surfaced only via an ACI partner listing). CIMA was the exception - confirmed in Slovenia only indirectly, through distributor Demi Trade's catalogue.

why_it_matters: These vendors may serve Slovenia from Austrian, Italian or Croatian hubs or through unnamed agents, meaning their Slovenian footprint is invisible on their own web properties and must be established through the company register (AJPES), bank locator/equipment evidence and tender awards instead of vendor sites. Treat as 'not yet evidenced', not as 'absent from the market'.

description: No public tender or contract-award document for any Slovenian bank's ATM fleet purchase, renewal or maintenance was found on the public procurement portal or elsewhere.

result.result_summary: Procurement searches returned only the ZJN-3 legal framework and unrelated contracting authorities. No bank ATM notices surfaced.

why_it_matters: This is structural, not a search failure: Slovenian commercial banks are private entities and not contracting authorities under ZJN-3, so their ATM and self-service purchases are never published. Competitive intelligence in this cell therefore cannot rely on procurement records for the bank channel and must be reconstructed from installed-base observation (ATMinfo/locator diffs), service-partner disclosure and vendor press. The exception worth monitoring is Posta Slovenije and other state-linked buyers, which the draft cash-access law would draw into the cash-point obligation.

description: No Slovenian bank was found publishing the identity of its ATM hardware or service supplier in any press release, annual report page or news article located in this pass, including for NLB, the largest fleet owner.

result.result_summary: Targeted Slovenian searches on NLB ATM procurement returned only locator pages, general terms and mobile-branch marketing - no supplier, contract or vendor name.

why_it_matters: Supplier attribution in this market must be inferred from second-order evidence: local service-partner customer logo walls (Demi Trade names NLB, NKBM, SKB and UniCredit), OEM press releases, and physical/photographic identification of machine models. Any vendor-share estimate built for Slovenia should be labelled as inferred, with its evidence chain recorded.

description: The Slovenian term 'bankomat' is heavily overloaded in consumer contexts and dominates search results with fee, locator and consumer-advice content, while the technically precise industry terms are far rarer.

result.result_summary: Consumer-facing pages crowded out supply-side results in nearly every 'bankomat' query. 'Recikliranje gotovine' as a Slovenian rendering of cash recycling returned essentially nothing supply-side; the market instead speaks of 'polog gotovine' and 'avtomatski polog'.

why_it_matters: Future collection should prefer the lower-noise supply-side vocabulary - 'bancni avtomat', 'upravljanje mreze bancnih avtomatov', 'samopostrezni terminal', 'bancna oprema', 'avtomatski polog gotovine', 'blagajniski sef', 'menjalni avtomat' - and should not expect a Slovenian-language equivalent of 'cash recycler' to exist as a marketing term.

description: Slovenian business press with the most likely supply-side reporting (Finance.si in particular) did not surface usable articles for this cell and is substantially subscription-gated.

result.result_summary: A targeted Finance.si-oriented query returned Delo, Monitor and Microsoft marketing pages instead of Finance.si articles, indicating either weak indexing or paywall exclusion.

why_it_matters: Finance.si and similar B2B outlets are the most likely place a Slovenian bank's technology investment or supplier switch would be reported. A subscription and manual archive search should be treated as a required capability for this cell rather than assuming open-web coverage is sufficient.

description: No Slovenian banking references found for Marand d.o.o. Two searches (sl: 'Marand banka rešitve reference slovenska banka projekt'; sl/en: 'Marand d.o.o. reference finance bančništvo Nova KBM OR NLB rešitev') returned only generic bank pages and one marketing-agency client list mentioning Marand Inženiring.

result.result_summary: Marand's public footprint in search does not include a banking vertical; its visible positioning is engineering and health informatics.

why_it_matters: The cell brief lists Marand as a bank-serving IT house. If that is wrong, tracking effort should be reallocated to Hrc, Halcom, SRC and Bankart, which do have evidenced bank relationships.

description: No company named 'Result d.o.o.' with a Slovenian banking practice could be located. The sl query 'Result d.o.o. banka rešitve reference Slovenija bančništvo' returned only bank websites, a Wikipedia bank list and — usefully — Hrc/Hibis. The name is also a highly noisy search term in Slovenian ('result' appears in unrelated contexts).

result.result_summary: Actor unconfirmed; possibly a mis-transcribed or renamed entity.

why_it_matters: Prevents an invented source entry, and flags that the actor list in the cell brief needs verification against AJPES/bizi before further searching.

description: Endava's Slovenian unit (Endava digitalne rešitve d.o.o., Ljubljana) publishes no client list or Slovenia-specific banking case studies discoverable via search; only entity data (address, ~231 staff, ~USD 36m sales) and a Facebook office post surfaced.

result.result_summary: Foreign-owned delivery centres in SI are opaque about which bank clients their local staff serve.

why_it_matters: Nearshore delivery centres are a real channel for foreign payments platforms into the region, but their SI footprint must be inferred from job ads and global case studies rather than a local reference page.

description: No Slovenian-language Comtrade site with a banking reference/customer page surfaced. Queries returned only registry aggregators (bizi.si, companywall.si) and a procurement supplier page. The group's regional banking material appears to live on non-SI Comtrade domains not reached in this pass.

result.result_summary: Comtrade's SI banking references are not directly discoverable from SI-scoped search; procurement records are the workable substitute.

why_it_matters: Comtrade is a large regional integrator; missing its reference page leaves a gap in the vendor-to-bank relationship map that must be closed via procurement and job-ad evidence.

description: Slovenian searches for Halcom project-level news ('Halcom novice reference banka implementacija ... digitalno bančništvo projekt') returned only product and about pages, not a datable newsroom index. A Halcom newsroom/press URL was therefore NOT recorded, to avoid inventing one.

result.result_summary: Halcom product and support pages are well indexed; its news/press stream is not, from search alone.

why_it_matters: Halcom is the highest-profile SI banking-software exporter; without a newsroom feed, deal announcements will be missed. A manual site-navigation pass is needed to locate the real press URL.

description: Several cell terms are noisy in Slovenian search: 'reference' also means bank account references and job references; 'banka' matches the bank's own marketing pages far more strongly than supplier pages; 'Result' and 'Špica' ('špica' = peak/rush hour) are common words. Company-name queries reliably return registry aggregators rather than the vendor's own site.

result.result_summary: Brand+topic queries in sl are dominated by bank sites and registry aggregators.

why_it_matters: Future collection should query with vendor-specific product names (Hibis, Hal E-Bank, bizBox, e-GenDoc, mIA, Kadris) rather than generic 'banka rešitve reference', which materially improves precision.

description: Bankart publishes no 'Partnerji' / 'Partners' or 'Reference' page, and no client-bank list. Repeated SL and EN queries for Bankart partner/technology pages returned only service, careers and news pages.

result.result_summary: The cell's expected 'partner/technology page' artefact does not exist for the single most important actor; partner identity must be reconstructed from news items, supplier case studies and owner-bank disclosures.

why_it_matters: Any collection design that assumes a scrapeable Bankart partner directory will silently return nothing; budget must move to supplier-side and press-release harvesting instead.

description: Searches for Bankart tenders/RFPs ('javno narocilo', 'razpis', 'dobavitelj') found no procurement notices. Bankart is a bank-owned private company and is not visible as a contracting authority on enarocanje.si in these results.

result.result_summary: No public tender trail for the country's main processor; its vendor purchases are commercially confidential.

why_it_matters: Bankart's supplier set can only be inferred indirectly (vendor case studies, trade press, job ads), so confidence on stack claims will stay medium at best.

description: The Flik participant-bank list is consistently referenced ('seznam bank najdete na www.flik.si') by Bankart and by member banks, but the exact URL of that list page was not isolated in this pass — only flik.si root and /pravne-osebe surfaced.

result.result_summary: Pointer confirmed to exist; its precise address unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: This list is the highest-value single artefact in the cell (full instant-payments participant graph); the next pass should crawl flik.si directly rather than rely on search.

description: Several Banka Slovenije payment-system pages surfaced on a staging-style host (bsi.azurewebsites.net) rather than www.bsi.si, and bsi.si URL paths appear in two forms (with and without an /sl/ segment).

result.result_summary: Canonical URLs for BSI payment-system pages are uncertain; some recorded URLs may redirect.

why_it_matters: Liveness verification may report false 404s for BSI paths; the verifier should follow redirects and treat the azurewebsites host as non-canonical.

description: No Slovenian-language term was found for a 'scheme technology partner programme' equivalent (e.g. certified-vendor / partner-programme listings) for Flik or the national rails; searches in SL returned only consumer and bank-facing content.

result.result_summary: The SI schemes appear not to run public certified-vendor programmes, unlike card schemes internationally.

why_it_matters: Vendor certification lists — a standard high-yield source type elsewhere — are likely absent for SI national schemes, and effort should not be spent hunting them.

description: No dedicated Slovenian fintech/payments industry association or member directory was located; searches for a 'Fintech Slovenija' association returned terminology pages and unrelated foreign fintech entries.

result.result_summary: Best available substitutes are the BSI registers plus the Startup.si ecosystem portal; no membership body page confirmed.

why_it_matters: Removes a normally high-yield pointer source (member lists, position papers, event agendas) for enumerating non-bank payment actors.

description: No Slovenian-language Nexi country site or local newsroom (e.g. a nexi.si equivalent to nexi.hr) was found in this pass; local presence surfaced only through company registries and the group site.

result.result_summary: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. confirmed as a registered entity (Letališka cesta 29A, Ljubljana; formerly Intesa Sanpaolo Card) but no local press room identified.

why_it_matters: Slovenian merchant announcements from the largest regional acquirer may only exist via partner banks' communications, requiring indirect monitoring.

description: No evidence found of Viva.com activity aimed at the Slovenian merchant market despite an explicit local-language query.

result.result_summary: Query returned SumUp and Revolut material only; Viva.com absent from results.

why_it_matters: Either a genuine coverage gap in this market or a search-recall failure; should not be read as absence of the player.

description: The Slovenian register of virtual-currency service providers (ponudniki storitev virtualnih valut) was referenced by a search result title but resolved only to the gov.si homepage.

result.result_summary: Register exists per result title; deep URL not obtained and not fabricated here.

why_it_matters: Needed to enumerate licensed crypto payment actors under the do_not_narrow instruction.

description: Signals conflict on mBills' operational status: the merchant-facing site is live while a FURS notice titled 'Prenehanje delovanja mBills' indicates removal as an eDavki payment option as of mid-2026.

result.result_summary: Recorded as an open question rather than a verdict; no source was fetched to confirm full wind-down.

why_it_matters: Whether the leading independent Slovenian wallet is exiting materially changes the competitive picture for bank wallets and Flik.

description: Across NLB, OTP banka, Gorenjska banka and Delavska hranilnica announcements surfaced in this run, the technology partner is usually NOT named. Banks describe the customer benefit ('prenovljena mobilna banka', 'nova izkušnja digitalnega bančništva') and omit the supplier.

result.result_summary: Searches combining bank names with 'v sodelovanju z' / 'in partnership with' returned launch stories but almost no explicit vendor attribution; the clearest exception was Addiko naming the state SI-PASS eID service.

why_it_matters: The buyer-side cell cannot be relied on alone for vendor attribution. It must be joined to vendor case studies (A6 vendor cell) and to procurement records, with the bank release supplying date and scope rather than the partner name.

description: Several smaller institutions (Primorska hranilnica Vipava, Deželna banka Slovenije, BKS Bank Slovenia branch, Hranilnica LON) surfaced with product and location pages but no discoverable press-release section in these searches.

result.result_summary: sl-language queries returned homepages, product pages and third-party aggregator profiles rather than any 'sporočila za javnost' or 'novice' index for these institutions.

why_it_matters: For the tail of the market, technology change must be inferred from product-page and T&C diffs rather than announcements — a different, slower collection method that must be planned for explicitly.

description: Nova KBM and SKB banka ceased to exist as brands and merged into OTP banka; Abanka, Sberbank/N Banka and Summit Leasing have likewise been absorbed. Their historical newsrooms are at risk of disappearing.

result.result_summary: Search results confirm the NKBM+SKB to OTP merger completion and the migration of customers to unified digital channels; legacy domains were not confirmed live in this run.

why_it_matters: Pre-merger go-live announcements are the record of which vendors those banks bought. If nkbm.si and skb.si are retired without archival, that history is lost — archive.org captures should be secured now.

description: Newsroom URLs for Banka Sparkasse (sparkasse.si), Hranilnica LON (lon.si), UniCredit Banka Slovenija and BKS Bank Slovenia were inferred from brand names and regulator register entries, not observed in search results.

result.result_summary: The Banka Slovenije supervised-entity register confirmed the legal entities exist; the corporate domains and their news paths were not directly observed.

why_it_matters: These must be resolved by the deterministic liveness pass before being treated as sources; recording them as confirmed would violate the no-fabrication rule.

description: No Slovenian bank technology/engineering blog (the kind that describes architecture and named platforms) was found in this run — neither in Slovenian nor English.

result.result_summary: Queries for bank digital-transformation pages returned marketing and strategy pages only; the nearest equivalent is the ZBS 'posvet informatikov' conference release and the SRC integrator magazine.

why_it_matters: Removes the richest potential buyer-side technical source category for this market. Conference proceedings and integrator publications must substitute.

description: Searches in Slovenian for municipal/state tenders using 'gotovinsko poslovanje', 'prevzem gotovine' and 'bančne storitve' returned consumer-banking and accounting content, not procurement notices.

result.result_summary: General web search does not index enarocanje.si notice bodies well; no cash-handling award notices were surfaced this way despite correct local-language terms.

why_it_matters: Confirms that keyword discovery must be run inside the portal / bulk datasets rather than via general web search; a general-search-only collector would systematically miss cash-handling and CIT contracts.

description: Fetch of the enarocanje.si homepage returned only the portal title; no search URL pattern, RSS feed, or export/API endpoint could be read from the landing page.

result.result_summary: Notice URL pattern (/Obrazci/?id_obrazec=NNNNNN) is known only from individual notices found via search engines. This is an unverified hypothesis about the site, not a verdict that no search exists.

why_it_matters: The collection design for the single most important source in this cell should not depend on scraping an undocumented UI; the OPSI bulk datasets are the safer enumeration route.

description: No dedicated Banka Slovenije procurement listing page was found; its FOI catalogue instead points to enarocanje.si as the publication venue.

result.result_summary: Central-bank procurements must be reached by filtering the national portal on naročnik, not by a bsi.si tender page.

why_it_matters: Avoids a wasted collector against a page that does not exist and pins the correct access route for the highest-value buyer in this cell.

description: English-language search for TED contract award notices covering Slovenian payment terminals / banking services returned platform documentation and unrelated notices, not SI-specific awards.

result.result_summary: TED content is not reliably discoverable through general web search; the Search API or on-site expert query is required.

why_it_matters: Sets the expectation that TED must be collected programmatically with country and CPV filters, not by keyword browsing.

description: No standalone, separately published Banka Slovenije register of payment-institution AGENTS (zastopniki) and hybrid payment institutions was located as its own URL. Local-language searching indicates agents are recorded as fields inside the payment-institution and e-money-institution registers rather than as a distinct public list.

result.result_summary: Searched 'register zastopnikov placilnih institucij' and 'hibridne placilne institucije seznam'; results returned only the master supervised-entities register, the non-bank PSP supervision hub and the ZPlaSS/ZPlaSSIED legal texts.

why_it_matters: The agent layer is where distribution partnerships live. If agent data is only embedded per-institution, collection must parse entity detail pages rather than a single list, which changes the extraction design.

description: The EBA central PSD2 register search application, the ECB SSM supervised-entities list, the ESMA MiCA register and the AJPES JOLP path were not directly confirmed by a fetched page in this run.

result.result_summary: These URLs are recorded from institutional design and prior knowledge rather than a confirmed search hit or fetch; the EBA search UI in particular is a JavaScript app that plain fetching may not render.

why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass must resolve these before they are treated as collectable. A failed fetch on them should be read as bot-defence/JS-rendering, not as a dead source.

description: Full bulk access to AJPES RTR and to aggregated financial data is not open data - it requires eRTR registration or a paid subscription under the AJPES price list, and natural-person accounts (type A) are legally excluded from publication.

result.result_summary: AJPES pages describe wsRtrInfoPs and bulk file subscription as reuse services with a cenik; only business-entity account data is public.

why_it_matters: Budget and a data-reuse agreement may be needed; personal-account data must never be collected, which constrains any account-level analysis to legal entities.

description: No Slovenian public register was found that enumerates POS/payment-terminal vendors, acquirers' technology suppliers or payment-software integrators as such - i.e. there is no licence list for the vendor side of the market.

result.result_summary: Searches for activity-based enumeration only lead back to AJPES SKD codes, which are a proxy, not a vendor register.

why_it_matters: The vendor universe cannot be built from a statutory list; it must be assembled from AJPES SKD filtering plus public procurement, bank tender awards and partner pages handled by other cells.

description: Statutory registers contain no case-study or partnership-narrative content whatsoever.

result.result_summary: All sources in this cell yield entity identity, licence scope and status only.

why_it_matters: The 'case studies' topic of this run cannot be served from cell 9; it must come from vendor/bank publication cells. Cell 9's contribution is the actor list those cells sample from.

description: No dedicated Slovenian FINTECH industry association with a public member directory was found. Searches in Slovenian for 'fintech združenje Slovenija' returned only blockchain/crypto bodies (Blockchain Alliance Europe, SBCA, Bitcoin društvo Slovenije), not a payments/fintech trade association comparable to e.g. Fintech Austria.

result.result_summary: Slovenian fintech interests appear to be represented indirectly, via ZBS (bank side), ZIT/GZS (ICT side) and blockchain alliances, rather than by a standalone fintech association.

why_it_matters: There is no single membership list that enumerates Slovenian fintech vendors; A6 vendor discovery must therefore triangulate ZIT + AmCham + DSI sponsors + blockchain alliances instead of relying on one roster.

description: ZBS publishes member logos but no public list of associate/affiliate or supplier members, and no public register of vendors participating in its committees or its education centre (Izobraževalni center) programmes was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: ZBS members page enumerates banks, savings banks and leasing companies only; the vendor-facing side of ZBS activity is not published as a directory.

why_it_matters: Bank–vendor working relationships visible through association committees must be recovered from event programmes and news items rather than a roster, raising collection cost.

description: GZS's company-data service indicates that basic company contact information is available only to GZS members; the AHK Slovenija online member directory may likewise be partly gated (not confirmed in this pass).

result.result_summary: Two of the largest chamber directories in scope may be membership-gated rather than openly crawlable.

why_it_matters: Budget or partnership decisions may be needed to obtain full chamber rosters; otherwise coverage skews toward associations with open directories (AmCham, BSCC, ZIT PDF).

description: The ZIT member-list PDF URL (04_Seznam članov_JULIJ 2026.pdf) was reported by a fetch of the ZIT Članstvo page but was not itself opened; its filename is date-stamped and will change when the roster is refreshed.

result.result_summary: URL recorded as a candidate with a note that the dated filename must be re-resolved from the parent page on each run.

why_it_matters: Hard-coding the dated PDF URL into a collector will silently break; the collector must resolve the link from the Članstvo page each time.

description: Foreign bilateral chambers beyond AmCham, AHK and BSCC (e.g. French, Italian, Nordic, Dutch chambers in Slovenia) were not searched in this pass due to cell time budget.

result.result_summary: Coverage of bilateral chambers is partial.

why_it_matters: Italian- and Austrian-origin vendors are commercially relevant to Slovenian banking given ownership structures (Intesa Sanpaolo, Sparkasse, BKS, Addiko); their chambers may hold directories not covered here.
